assessments.scoringCutoffs:
Each item rated 0 (Not at all) to 3 (Nearly every day); Total range 0–27.
Severity Cutoffs: 0–4 = Minimal/None | 5–9 = Mild | 10–14 = Moderate (clinical threshold) | 15–19 = Moderately Severe | 20–27 = Severe. Always check Item 9 for suicide/self-harm risk.
assessments.citation: Kroenke, K., Spitzer, R. L., & Williams, J. B. (2001). The PHQ-9: Validity of a brief depression severity measure. Journal of General Internal Medicine, 16(9), 606–613. https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1525-1497.2001.016009606.x

assessments.scoringCutoffs:
Each item rated 0 (Not at all) to 3 (Nearly every day); Total range 0–21.
Severity Cutoffs: 0–4 = Minimal | 5–9 = Mild | 10–14 = Moderate (clinical cutoff >=10) | 15–21 = Severe anxiety.
assessments.citation: Spitzer, R. L., Kroenke, K., Williams, J. B. W., & Löwe, B. (2006). A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: The GAD-7. Archives of Internal Medicine, 166(10), 1092–1097. https://doi.org/10.1001/archinte.166.10.1092

assessments.scoringCutoffs:
20 items rated 0 (Not at all) to 4 (Extremely); Total range 0–80.
Clinical Cutoff: A total score of 31–33 or higher suggests probable PTSD. DSM-5 cluster scoring: at least 1 Cluster B item (1–5), 1 Cluster C item (6–7), 2 Cluster D items (8–14), and 2 Cluster E items (15–20) rated >=2 ('Moderately').
assessments.citation: Weathers, F. W., Litz, B. T., Keane, T. M., Palmieri, P. A., Marx, B. P., & Schnurr, P. P. (2013). The PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). National Center for PTSD. https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/adult-sr/ptsd-checklist.asp

assessments.scoringCutoffs: PTSD symptoms are Items 1–6 (with functional impairment Items 7–9), and Disturbances in Self-Organization (DSO: Affect Dysregulation, Negative Self-Concept, Relational Disturbance) are Items 10–15 (with functional impairment Items 16–18), all rated 0–4. A symptom cluster is endorsed when at least one item is >=2 ('Moderately'), and diagnosis also requires functional impairment.
assessments.citation: Cloitre, M., Shevlin, M., Brewin, C. R., Bisson, J. I., Roberts, N. P., Maercker, A., Karatzias, T., & Hyland, P. (2018). The International Trauma Questionnaire: Development of a self-report measure of ICD-11 PTSD and complex PTSD. Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica, 138(6), 536–546. https://doi.org/10.1111/acps.12956

assessments.scoringCutoffs:
28 items rated 0% to 100% (in 10% increments). Total score is the average across all 28 items (sum divided by 28; range 0–100).
Cutoffs: Mean score >=30 indicates high dissociation warranting structured clinical assessment for PTSD or a Dissociative Disorder.
assessments.citation: Carlson, E. B., & Putnam, F. W. (1993). An update on the Dissociative Experiences Scale. Dissociation: Progress in the Dissociative Disorders, 6(1), 16–27.

diagnoses: Z62.81x Personal History of Abuse in Childhood
assessments.scoringCutoffs: 10 Yes/No items covering experiences before age 18 (Range 0–10). Scores >=4 are associated with significantly elevated risk for chronic health and trauma-related conditions; always pair with a Protective/Resilience Questionnaire (e.g., BCEs).
assessments.citation: Felitti, V. J., Anda, R. F., Nordenberg, D., Williamson, D. F., Spitz, A. M., Edwards, V., Koss, M. P., & Marks, J. S. (1998). Relationship of childhood abuse and household dysfunction to many of the leading causes of death in adults: The Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACE) Study. American Journal of Preventive Medicine, 14(4), 245–258. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0749-3797(98)00017-8

assessments.scoringCutoffs: Part A (Items 1–6) is the core screener: 4 or more marks in the shaded boxes (Sometimes/Often/Very Often for Items 1–3; Often/Very Often for Items 4–6) is highly consistent with Adult ADHD and warrants comprehensive diagnostic evaluation. Part B (Items 7–18) provides additional symptom context.
assessments.citation: Kessler, R. C., Adler, L., Ames, M., Demler, O., Faraone, S., Hiripi, E., Howes, M. J., Jin, R., Secnik, K., Spencer, T., Ustun, T. B., & Walters, E. E. (2005). The World Health Organization Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS): A short screening scale for use in the general population. Psychological Medicine, 35(2), 245–256. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0033291704002892

assessments.scoringCutoffs: AQ-50 Range: 0–50 (Clinical threshold >=26 in clinical referrals; >=32 in general population). AQ-10 Range: 0–10 (Cutoff >=6 indicates referral for comprehensive autism evaluation).
assessments.citation: Baron-Cohen, S., Wheelwright, S., Skinner, R., Martin, J., & Clubley, E. (2001). The Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ): Evidence from Asperger syndrome/high-functioning autism, males and females, scientists and mathematicians. Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders, 31(1), 5–17. https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1005653411471

assessments.scoringCutoffs:
25 items rated 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 7 (Strongly Agree); Total range 25–175 across 3 subscales: Compensation, Masking, and Assimilation.
No validated clinical cutoff: Hull et al. (2019) did not set one. Higher totals reflect more social camouflaging/masking, and >=100 is sometimes used informally as a guide (especially valuable for late-identified women, AFAB, and gender-diverse adults).
assessments.citation: Hull, L., Mandy, W., Lai, M.-C., Baron-Cohen, S., Allison, C., Smith, P., & Petrides, K. V. (2019). Development and validation of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q). Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders, 49(3), 819–833. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10803-018-3792-6

assessments.scoringCutoffs: 80 items across 4 domains (Social Relatedness, Circumscribed Interests, Language, Sensory-Motor); Total range 0–240. Threshold score >=65 supports autistic neurotype when interpreted alongside developmental history.
assessments.citation: Ritvo, R. A., Ritvo, E. R., Guthrie, D., Ritvo, M. J., Hufnagel, D. H., McMahon, W., Tonge, B., Mataix-Cols, D., Jassi, A., Attwood, T., & Eloff, J. (2011). The Ritvo Autism Asperger Diagnostic Scale-Revised (RAADS-R): A scale to assist the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in adults: An international validation study. Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders, 41(8), 1076–1089. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10803-010-1133-5

assessments.scoringCutoffs:
OCI-R: 18 items rated 0–4 (Total 0–72); Clinical cutoff >=21 indicates likely OCD.
Y-BOCS Severity Scale (10 items rated 0–4; Total 0–40): 0–7 = Subclinical | 8–15 = Mild | 16–23 = Moderate | 24–31 = Severe | 32–40 = Extreme.
assessments.citation: Foa, E. B., Huppert, J. D., Leiberg, S., Langner, R., Kichic, R., Hajcak, G., & Salkovskis, P. M. (2002). The Obsessive-Compulsive Inventory: Development and validation of a short version. Psychological Assessment, 14(4), 485–496. https://doi.org/10.1037/1040-3590.14.4.485

assessments.scoringCutoffs: Positive screen requires ALL THREE criteria: (1) 7 or more 'Yes' responses on the 13 symptom items in Question 1, (2) 'Yes' on Question 2 (several symptoms occurred during the same period), AND (3) 'Moderate' or 'Serious' problem on Question 3.
assessments.citation: Hirschfeld, R. M. A., Williams, J. B. W., Spitzer, R. L., Calabrese, J. R., Flynn, L., Keck, P. E., Jr., Lewis, L., McElroy, S. L., Post, R. M., Rapport, D. J., Russell, J. M., Sachs, G. S., & Zajecka, J. (2000). Development and validation of a screening instrument for bipolar spectrum disorder: The Mood Disorder Questionnaire. American Journal of Psychiatry, 157(11), 1873–1875. https://doi.org/10.1176/appi.ajp.157.11.1873

assessments.scoringCutoffs: Items 1–2 = Low/Moderate risk (depending on frequency) | Item 3 (Thoughts of method without specific plan/intent) = Moderate Risk | Items 4 or 5 in the past month (Intent, or Intent with Plan) or Item 6 in the past 3 months (Suicidal Behavior) = High / Acute Risk requiring immediate safety planning.
assessments.citation: Posner, K., Brown, G. K., Stanley, B., Brent, D. A., Yershova, K. V., Oquendo, M. A., Currier, G. W., Melvin, G. A., Greenhill, L., Shen, S., & Mann, J. J. (2011). The Columbia–Suicide Severity Rating Scale: Initial validity and internal consistency findings from three multisite studies with adolescents and adults. American Journal of Psychiatry, 168(12), 1266–1277. https://doi.org/10.1176/appi.ajp.2011.10111704

assessments.fullName: Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test & Drug Abuse Screening Test
assessments.scoringCutoffs:
AUDIT (0–40, WHO zones): 0–7 = Low risk | 8–15 = Hazardous use | 16–19 = Harmful use | 20–40 = Possible alcohol dependence.
DAST-10 (0–10): 0 = None | 1–2 = Low | 3–5 = Moderate | 6–8 = Substantial | 9–10 = Severe.
assessments.citation: Saunders, J. B., Aasland, O. G., Babor, T. F., de la Fuente, J. R., & Grant, M. (1993). Development of the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT): WHO Collaborative Project on Early Detection of Persons with Harmful Alcohol Consumption—II. Addiction, 88(6), 791–804. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1360-0443.1993.tb02093.x

assessments.fullName: Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire & Nine Item ARFID Screen
assessments.scoringCutoffs:
EDE-Q (0–6 scale across 4 subscales): Global score >=2.3–2.8 indicates clinically significant disordered eating.
NIAS (9 items rated 0–5 across Picky/Sensory, Appetite, and Fear subscales): Subscale cutoffs >=10 (Picky), >=9 (Appetite), >=10 (Fear) indicate positive ARFID screen.
assessments.citation: Fairburn, C. G., & Beglin, S. J. (1994). Assessment of eating disorders: Interview or self-report questionnaire? International Journal of Eating Disorders, 16(4), 363–370. https://doi.org/10.1002/1098-108X(199412)16:4<363::AID-EAT2260160405>3.0.CO;2-#

assessments.fullName: Revised Child Anxiety and Depression Scale & NICHQ Vanderbilt Assessment
assessments.scoringCutoffs:
RCADS converts raw scores to age/grade T-scores: T-score >=65 = Borderline clinical | T-score >=70 = Clinical threshold.
NICHQ Vanderbilt: Requires >=6 of 9 Inattentive or Hyperactive items scored 2 ('Often') or 3 ('Very Often') plus performance impairment score of 4 or 5.
assessments.citation: Chorpita, B. F., Yim, L., Moffitt, C., Umemoto, L. A., & Francis, S. E. (2000). Assessment of symptoms of DSM-IV anxiety and depression in children: A revised child anxiety and depression scale. Behaviour Research and Therapy, 38(8), 835–855. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0005-7967(99)00130-8

assessments.fullName: WHO Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 & DSM-5-TR Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure
assessments.scoringCutoffs:
WHODAS 2.0 (12-Item): Items rated 1 (None) to 5 (Extreme/Cannot do) over past 30 days; documents functional disability for insurance medical necessity.
DSM-5-TR Level 1: Any item rated >=2 ('Mild' or greater; >=1 for suicide/psychosis/substance items) prompts deeper Level 2 assessment.
assessments.citation: Üstün, T. B., Chatterji, S., Kostanjsek, N., Rehm, J., Kennedy, C., Epping-Jordan, J., Saxena, S., von Korff, M., & Pull, C. (2010). Developing the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0. Bulletin of the World Health Organization, 88(11), 815–823. https://doi.org/10.2471/BLT.09.067231
